key_insight: Muon can substantially improve agentic reinforcement learning when used selectively: in sparse-reward RL on ALFWorld, applying Muon only to hidden weight matrices nearly doubled final validation success versus AdamW. The paper shows Muon’s benefit is context-dependent rather than universally better across all RL settings.
problem_solved: The paper addresses whether Muon, which is strong in large-scale pre-training, also helps during RL post-training for agentic tasks with sparse rewards. It specifically tests if Muon can overcome the instability and weak learning progress often seen in such RL setups.
method: Matched single-seed comparisons of Muon vs. AdamW on ALFWorld with Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct.
Use of Group-in-Group Policy Optimization (GiGPO) as the RL training framework.
Applying Muon only to hidden weight matrices while keeping other settings controlled, then comparing validation success and post-update behavior.
impact: For practitioners, this suggests optimizer choice can materially affect RL fine-tuning performance, especially in sparse-reward agentic environments. It also highlights that partial optimizer substitution may deliver gains without changing the entire training stack.
visual_elements: Side-by-side optimizer comparison chart: Muon vs. AdamW success rates.
Training pipeline diagram showing GiGPO with Muon applied only to hidden weight matrices.
Timeline or line plot of validation success over training windows.
Icon set for sparse rewards, optimizer swap, and agentic task completion.
paper_title: When Does Muon Help Agentic Reinforcement Learning?
paper_authors: Kai Ruan, Jinghao Lin, Zihe Huang, Ziqi Zhou, Qianshan Wei
